title: Saturable nonlinear Schrödinger equation with space- and time-dependent variable coefficients
authors: Maurilho R. da Rocha, Mateus C. P. dos Santos, Wesley B. Cardoso
abstract: In this paper we study the dynamics and stability of localized solutions in a saturable nonlinear Schrödinger equation with space- and time-dependent variable coefficients. Using a variational approach and numerical simulations, we analyze the effects of different external potential configurations. Our results reveal that the stability of the solutions is highly sensitive to the modulation parameters, leading to the emergence of alternating stable and unstable regions as a function of the modulation frequency. These findings provide valuable insights into the control of localized structures in nonlinear wave systems, with potential implications for optical waveguides, Bose-Einstein condensates, and other nonlinear media.
summary: This paper analyzes the stability and dynamics of localized wave packets governed by a saturable nonlinear Schrödinger equation with time- and space-dependent coefficients. Using variational methods and numerical simulations, the authors demonstrate that the stability of these structures is critically dependent on the modulation parameters. The findings offer crucial insights for controlling nonlinear wave phenomena in physical media.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamics and stability of localized solutions within a saturable nonlinear Schrödinger equation featuring space- and time-dependent variable coefficients.
main_result: The stability of the localized solutions is found to be highly sensitive to the modulation parameters, leading to the emergence of alternating stable and unstable regions.
method: The research employs a combination of variational approaches, similarity transformations to achieve autonomous forms, and linear stability analysis via an eigenvalue problem, supplemented by direct numerical simulations.
model_or_system: The core model is the saturable nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLS) with the general form $i\psi_t = - rac{1}{2}\psi_{xx} + V(x, t)\psi + g(x, t)|\psi|^2\psi + \gamma(x, t)|\psi|^2$. The analysis explores various non-autonomous potentials, including static, seesaw, flying-bird, and mixed potentials.
key_observables: Stability (determined by the sign of the eigenvalue $\lambda$), maximum amplitude ($h_{	ext{max}}$), and mean width ($\langle x^2 angle$).
important_parameters: Modulation parameters (e.g., modulation frequency $\omega_0$, and parameters $\sigma$ used in potentials), and variational parameters $A$ and $B$.
main_assumptions: The variational method relies on a Taylor series expansion for the logarithmic term, and the stability analysis for the autonomous case is separate from the full non-autonomous system.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the real part of the eigenvalue $\lambda$ vs. energy $E$ for the autonomous case, and show the evolution of $h_{	ext{max}}$ and $\langle x^2 angle$ for various modulation potentials (static, seesaw, flying-bird, mixed) as a function of modulation frequency $\omega_0$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general NLS model and applying variational/similarity techniques to derive an autonomous form. It then analyzes stability using eigenvalue problems and concludes with direct numerical simulations testing various time-dependent potentials to map out stability regimes.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics as the NLS equation is a canonical model for describing nonlinear wave propagation in systems like optical waveguides and Bose-Einstein condensates.
